subject.title: Synchronous transcript I/O scales with tool-result payload size and can block the event loop the liveness monitor samples

question: Is the source-level evidence enough to sponsor a transcript-persistence refactor now, or should maintainers require a current-main large-tool-output/liveness measurement first?
rationale: The source still contains synchronous transcript writes, but the reported raw-payload reproduction may already be bounded by current tool-result truncation, so the safest scope depends on maintainer confidence in the remaining real-world stall risk.

options.title: Measure Current Main First
options.body: Capture eventLoopDelayMaxMs and recovery behavior for a large guarded tool result before authorizing a persistence refactor.

options.title: Sponsor Async Persistence Refactor
options.body: Treat the source-level synchronous hot path as sufficient and ask for a bounded design that preserves locks, snapshots, and transcript branch semantics.

options.title: Fold Into Liveness Canonical Work
options.body: Track this only as supporting evidence for the broader stuck-session recovery issues if maintainers do not want a separate transcript I/O item.

recommendation.title: Measure Current Main First
recommendation.body: Capture eventLoopDelayMaxMs and recovery behavior for a large guarded tool result before authorizing a persistence refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the clearest current-history owner for both the transcript hot path and the shipped tool-result cap context in this checkout.
